$comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the sourcetype -> catalog-key alias map.
Consumed by BOTH src/bundled-data.ts (iframe) and scripts/reference-api.mjs (standalone backend).
These two used to hold hand-mirrored copies and DRIFTED: bundled-data was missing alibaba_action_trail
entirely, and still carried the buggy bare-`audit` alias that reference-api had already fixed — so the
same sourcetype resolved a different sample depending on run mode. Add aliases HERE only.
Values are catalog-key substrings, matched case-insensitively; order matters (richest/most-relevant first).
`storeKeys` is a SECOND, different map: exact store keys — the samples pool manifest and config/ai-samples/.
It is deliberately NOT the substring map above — a store lookup is file equality, so a loose pattern
there would either silently miss or, worse, serve a neighbouring product's real log as if it were ours
(cisco_firepower's `ftd` pattern would hand back cisco_ftd.json). One entry per source, exact keys only,
and every entry states which real file it points at and why the two names are the same source.

$notes.linux_audit: NOT a bare 'audit' — that substring greedily matches 40+ unrelated catalog keys (cyberark sample-audit, slack/hubspot/openai/netskope audit logs) and there is NO real linux auditd sample in the catalog, so 'audit' could only ever resolve the WRONG source. (Bug: linux_audit pulled cyberark IDP JSON into a LinuxAudit_CIM pack.) Keep only precise, auditd-specific keys.
$notes.zscaler_web: Precise: zscaler_web_logs is the real JSON web-transaction sample (20 events). A bare 'zscaler' also pulls ZPA/ZIA/firewall/LEEF variants that are NOT web proxy logs; keep it targeted so the web pack gets the web sample.
$notes.zscaler:nssweblog: zscaler:nssweblog (Splunk NSS web-transaction sourcetype) IS the zscaler_web JSON format — point it at the same real 20-event sample rather than letting it fall to AI.
$notes.infoblox_dns: DNS-specific — a bare 'infoblox' greedily matches dhcp/ntpd/leef/audit/etc.
$notes.corelight_conn: Corelight/Zeek conn logs — target the cl_conn keys (20-event CL_Conn_300), NOT a bare 'corelight' (matches ccs_threat_info_corelight_notice, 1 event). Corelight is a commercial Zeek distro, so zeek_conn resolves the same sample.

$storeNotes.ncsc_cloudflare_device_posture: The customer census spells Cloudflare's Logpush device-posture feed with the collecting team's `ncsc_` prefix. cloudflare_logpush_device_posture.json holds the real PascalCase Logpush events for exactly that dataset — and until this alias existed the generated sample shadowed them, which is how a fabricated device-posture sample reached the review queue with a structure-only pass.
$storeNotes.ncsc_cloudflare_dns: Authoritative-DNS Logpush dataset. Same `ncsc_` prefix story as device_posture; all seven Cloudflare feeds below had a real Logpush fixture sitting unread on disk while a generated sample was promoted for the same source.
$storeNotes.ncsc_cloudflare_firewall: Logpush calls this dataset `firewall_event` (singular event), which is why the prefixed name misses it on an exact lookup.
$storeNotes.ncsc_cloudflare_gateway_dns: Zero Trust Gateway DNS queries — a different dataset from the authoritative-DNS one above, so the two aliases must stay separate.
$storeNotes.ncsc_cloudflare_gateway_http: Zero Trust Gateway HTTP requests — again distinct from the CDN `http_request` dataset below.
$storeNotes.ncsc_cloudflare_gateway_network: Zero Trust Gateway L4 network sessions.
$storeNotes.ncsc_cloudflare_http: The CDN/WAF request log; Logpush names the dataset `http_request`.
$storeNotes.ncsc_cloudflare_ztna: ZTNA is Cloudflare Access, whose Logpush dataset is `access_request` — the only mapping in this group inferred from the product name rather than a matching dataset name, so if the customer's ZTNA feed turns out to be gateway traffic rather than Access logins, this is the entry to re-check.
$storeNotes.mscs_azure_eventhub: `mscs_` is the collecting team's prefix for Microsoft Cloud Services; the feed itself is Azure Event Hub, whose real events are in azure_eventhub.json.
$storeNotes.juniper_junos_firewall: Junos firewall events are Junos syslog — juniper_junos.json is the same wire format. NOT juniper_srx: that is a specific platform's own sample and would silently substitute one product's log for another.
$storeNotes.aws_vpc_v5: Canonical parser name is aws_vpc_v5; the vendor-samples store key is aws_vpcflow (Elastic corpus spelling). Without this alias, batch rows for aws_vpc_v5 parked as 'Needs sample' while the real flow-log fixture sat unread.
$storeNotes.aws_vpc_flow: Alias form used in catalogs / CSV shorthand; same aws_vpcflow fixture as aws_vpc_v5.
$storeNotes.aws_vpc_v2: v2 layout still uses the same space-separated VPC Flow fixture for sample resolution; the parser case handles column differences.
